summary: Frontend-only E2E and code review completed for Monthly Comparison and Recurring Transactions on the public URL at mobile 390x844 and desktop 1920x1080. Comparison values/chart/color logic and recurring CRUD, validation, persistence, auto-apply data mutation, idempotency, active state, expense category requirement, and category cascade passed. Two user-facing defects were reproduced: auto-apply never shows its required success toast, and the fixed FAB can overlap the recurring Delete target on mobile.

ui_bugs.issue: At 390x844, when the recurring item is scrolled into view near the bottom, the fixed FAB overlays the center of its Delete button. elementFromPoint at the Delete center resolves to fab-toggle; tapping there opens the FAB menu instead of the delete confirmation. The recurring row also measured 311px scrollWidth in a 306px clientWidth.

integration_issues.issue: The pending recurring income is created and lastAppliedMonth is persisted, but the required 'Se aplicaron 1 transacción(es) recurrente(s) de este mes.' toast never appears. Reproduced twice with dayOfMonth=1 and lastAppliedMonth=null.

issues: The fixed FAB can cover a recurring row action at reachable scroll positions; the row has a small 5px internal horizontal overflow.
The prompt says associated expenses will be deleted but does not disclose that linked recurring expense schedules are also permanently removed by the new cascade.

action_items: Refactor applyPendingRecurring so its applied count is computed synchronously/purely before the state update (or expose a post-update result), allowing FinanceApp to show the required success toast.

Prevent QuickAddFAB from covering recurring action buttons on mobile, for example with sufficient content safe-area spacing or collision-aware placement; eliminate the recurring-row internal overflow.
Update the category deletion confirmation to explicitly mention deletion of linked recurring expense schedules.
critical_code_review_comments: useFinance.applyPendingRecurring mutates appliedCount inside a setData functional updater and immediately returns it. React executes the queued updater after the callback has returned, so FinanceApp receives 0 even though data is later applied; this is the root cause of the missing toast.

The applyPendingRecurring state updater is impure: it mutates an outer variable and generates random IDs. React Strict Mode may invoke updater functions more than once, so eligibility/count/ID generation should be moved into a pure deterministic calculation.
QuickAddFAB uses fixed bottom-6 z-50 positioning without preventing collision with page controls. At the reproduced scroll position, its hit area wins over the recurring Delete button.
Categories.handleDelete has stale confirmation copy after adding the recurring cascade and does not warn users that a recurring schedule will be deleted.
seed_data_creation: Used isolated localStorage fixtures under finance_tracker_data_v1 for Jan/Feb 2026 comparison data, recurring income/expense schedules, active/idempotency states, and cascade testing. UI-created recurring records were deleted during the flows; no backend/shared data was modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Retest the auto-apply toast with dayOfMonth=1 and lastAppliedMonth=null, then reload to confirm exactly one transaction and no second toast. At 390x844, place a recurring item around y=733-795: previously Delete center (x=339,y=764) hit fab-toggle and opened the FAB menu. All comparison assertions passed: Jan 30000/2000 vs Feb 32000/2500 produced +6.7%, +25.0%, +5.4%, six chart bars, and correct inverted expense colors. Recurring create/edit/delete/toggle/validation/category cascade and desktop rendering passed.
rca_of_the_issue: Missing toast: applyPendingRecurring returns appliedCount before React runs the setData updater that increments it, so FinanceApp sees zero and skips toast.success. Mobile obstruction: the z-50 fixed FAB overlaps a visible recurring Delete hit target at certain scroll offsets; a center tap is routed to fab-toggle.
